feasibility_verdict.headline: INCREASING BUDGETS ALONE WILL NOT PRODUCE $13,000 OF AUGUST SPEND.
reasoning: Four of the five campaigns report 0.00% search lost impression share from budget. For those four, budget is not the constraint and raising it cannot by itself buy a single extra impression.
The same four report 63% to 87% search lost impression share from rank, or in Gas Boiler Repair's case no eligible auction at all.
Only HVAC Installation is genuinely budget-limited, at 32.47% month to date and 53.01% today. Its increase is the one that should convert almost fully.

Of the $569.58 per day of proposed increase, roughly $184 (HVAC Installation) is well supported by evidence and roughly $188 (AC Repair) is partly supported. The remaining ~$197 across HVAC Repair, HVAC Replacement and Gas Boiler Repair is expected to sit unspent.

Total eligible impressions across the five since launch are about 3,021, roughly 500 a day. At the observed 2.72% click-through rate and $43.05 cost per click, even 100% impression share is worth only about $590 a day at today's prices.
feasibility_verdict.what_would_actually_raise_spend: Only a broader keyword footprint, a higher bid ceiling, additional services or additional geography would raise eligible auction volume. Every one of those is explicitly out of scope for this task and none is proposed.
feasibility_verdict.no_promise: This package does not promise that Google will spend $13,000. It sets budgets so that budget is never the limiting factor, and states plainly that auction demand will decide the outcome.

maximum_possible_daily_overdelivery.rule: Google may spend up to 2x a campaign's daily budget on any individual day, balancing across the month.
maximum_possible_daily_overdelivery.interpretation: This arithmetic ceiling is far above the $13,000 cap. Google's own monthly charging limit is computed per campaign from the daily budget in effect and is recalculated when a budget changes mid-month, so it cannot be relied on to hold this account to $13,000. Observed demand makes the ceiling unreachable in practice, but the only dependable safeguard is the daily pacing check below.

cpc_inflation.observation: Average cost per click is already $43.05 across the five, and $70.52 on AC Repair today, with zero recorded leads.
cpc_inflation.mechanism: Under TARGET_SPEND (Maximize Clicks) with no cpc_bid_ceiling, raising the budget is functionally an instruction to bid harder. A 2.33x budget on a rank-limited campaign is likely to raise cost per click rather than click volume.
cpc_inflation.recommended_guard_NOT_INCLUDED: Setting campaign.target_spend.cpc_bid_ceiling_micros on AC Repair and HVAC Installation would cap that inflation without changing the bidding strategy type. It is a bidding-configuration change, it is outside the budgets-only scope of this package, and it is NOT in this fingerprint. It needs its own approval and its own fingerprint if wanted.

risks.measurement: Zero primary conversions are recorded. Spending to a $13,000 cap while no lead event reaches Google Ads means the money buys clicks with no measurable outcome. Fixing the WhatConverts-to-Google-Ads upload mapping is out of scope here and is flagged, not actioned.
